expectations.text: Corrects the claim that GraphQL forbids versioning, stating the paradigm does not dictate versioning policy.
expectations.evidence: "'GraphQL has no versions' is wrong... The paradigm doesn't decide the policy."

expectations.text: Names Shopify's quarterly date-based versioning of its GraphQL Admin API as the counter-example.
expectations.evidence: "Shopify ships date-based versions of its GraphQL Admin API every quarter"

expectations.text: Records which versioning stance the team takes and hands the ongoing policy - notice periods, deprecation workflow, removal discipline - to versioning-policy work rather than settling it here.

expectations.text: Rejects `Int` for identifiers and requires the `ID` scalar.
expectations.evidence: "Use id: ID! on a Node interface"

expectations.text: Requires a `Node` interface (`interface Node { id: ID! }`) on every entity so any object is refetchable by one global ID.

expectations.text: Requires IDs to be opaque to clients, base64-encoding compound identities rather than exposing raw numeric primary keys.

expectations.text: States the design goal of that migration: any consumer that never persisted a global ID needs no changes at all.
